documentControl.title: Tumor Evaluation Review Agent (TEA) — Development Plan
documentControl.effectiveDate: Upon sponsor approval of Step 1 gate
documentControl.author: Claude Code session

intendedAudience.audience: Clinical Data Management (data reviewers, data managers)

changeHistory.revision: Initial draft covering agent concept, data model, review scope, architecture, web application concept, six-step delivery plan, requirements, risks, validation approach, version control policy, recommendations and open questions.

documentControl.versioningPolicy: Semantic versioning per artifact; filenames are version-free and versions live in the document plus a git tag. Rule pack, prompts and engine are versioned independently of the documents. Every agent output carries a provenance stamp naming all of them. See docs/README.md for the full policy.

executiveSummary.paragraph: Tumor evaluation data is among the highest-risk and lowest-automation areas of oncology data review. The efficacy endpoint of most oncology trials (ORR, PFS, DoR, BOR) is derived from lesion-level measurements and investigator response assessments that are entered by site staff, change frequently as scans are re-read, and must obey a dense set of rules from RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST plus protocol-specific deviations. Manual review is performed by Clinical Data Managers and Medical Monitors listing-by-listing, is repeated at every data cut, and does not scale with the volume or the change rate of the data.

The Tumor Evaluation Review Agent (TEA) is a decision-support agent that re-derives every RECIST/iRECIST quantity from the collected lesion data, compares the derivation with what the site reported, cross-checks the result against the query history, and produces a prioritised list of suspicious issues. Each issue is presented with five reviewer-facing elements: what review point was checked, what the issue is and on which data, why it is an issue (with current vs expected values), a suggested initial query text, and additional information (review tips and guideline background). Findings are surfaced in a purpose-built web application whose interaction model follows the conventions of established clinical data review platforms.

The central architectural commitment is deterministic-first: all arithmetic and all rule verdicts are produced by a versioned, testable rule engine, never by a language model. The LLM is used only where judgement or language is genuinely required — narrative adjudication of ambiguous cases, reconciliation of free-text query answers, and generation of reviewer-facing explanations and query drafts. This keeps the system reproducible and validatable under GxP, and makes the agent portable across a commercial API model and a company-hosted local model (notably GLM) without any change to the review verdicts themselves.

problemStatement.painPoint: Review frequency versus data volume: lesion data arrives continuously, and a full manual re-review at every data cut is impractical, so review is sampled or deferred and issues are found late — often at database lock or at the point of endpoint derivation.

Rule complexity: correct application of RECIST 1.1 requires simultaneous reasoning over lesion measurability, target selection constraints, nodal short-axis handling, nadir tracking, the overall response table, confirmation rules, and best-overall-response derivation. Reviewers cannot hold all of this in mind while reading listings.

Exceptional cases dominate the risk: lesions that disappear and reappear, lesions too small to measure, non-evaluable timepoints, irradiated or locally treated lesions, unequivocal non-target progression, new lesions in regions not imaged at baseline, pseudoprogression under immunotherapy. These are precisely the cases that manual checklists miss.
Query history is disconnected from review: reviewers re-raise queries that were already asked and answered, or fail to notice that a query was answered without the data actually being corrected.

Knowledge asymmetry: junior data managers can detect an arithmetic mismatch but cannot judge whether an assessment is clinically defensible; medical monitors have the judgement but not the time to scan every record.
Traceability: when an issue is raised, the reasoning is rarely captured in a form that survives to inspection, so the same discussion is repeated at the next data cut.
problemStatement.currentStateNotes: Existing tooling in this space (EDC edit checks, listings review, statistical monitoring) catches field-level and cross-field errors but does not carry a guideline model. Edit checks are per-form and per-visit; RECIST logic is longitudinal (nadir, confirmation, BOR) and therefore falls outside what an EDC check can express.

objectives.objective: Re-derive, for every subject and timepoint, the sum of diameters, percent change from baseline and from nadir, target response, non-target response, new-lesion status, overall timepoint response, and best overall response — under the guideline version and protocol parameters that apply to the study.

Detect and report discrepancies between derived values and collected values, plus guideline-conformance issues that are not simple mismatches (e.g. ineligible target lesion selection, missing confirmation assessment).
Present each issue with the five reviewer-facing elements (review point, issue and data location, reason with current-vs-expected, suggested query text, additional information).
Suppress or down-rank issues already covered by the query history; escalate issues where a query was closed but the underlying data still fails the check.
Run against a commercial LLM API and a company-hosted local LLM (GLM family) with identical review verdicts and no code changes beyond configuration.
Support RECIST 1.0, RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST as selectable, versioned rule packs; be extensible to indication-specific criteria without touching the engine.
Provide a holistic review environment: subject-level timelines, cross-subject and cross-site issue patterns, and saved reviewer worklists, not just a flat issue list.
Achieve a false-positive rate low enough that reviewers trust the output; target and measurement stated in .
Be maintainable by a clinical programming team: adding a new review point is a self-contained, declarative change with its own tests, requiring no change to the engine.

inScope.item: Solid-tumor response assessment data collected under RECIST 1.0, RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST.
Investigator assessments; and, where collected, independent central review (BICR) assessments and investigator-vs-BICR reconciliation flags.
Lesion-level identification and measurement data, timepoint response data, best overall response, progression dates.
Query history (issued queries and their answers) as a second input stream.

Supporting cross-domain data used for consistency checks: visit dates, exposure/first dose, disposition, death date, anticancer therapy, radiotherapy/surgery, adverse events indicating disease progression.
A web application presenting the agent output for human review and query drafting.

outOfScope.item: Reading or interpreting the images themselves. TEA reviews the recorded data, not DICOM.
Automatic posting of queries into the EDC without human approval (see ).

Non-solid-tumor criteria (Lugano/lymphoma, IMWG/myeloma, PCWG3/prostate, RANO/CNS) and modality-specific variants (mRECIST for HCC, Choi for GIST) in the first release; the rule pack mechanism is designed to accept them later.
Endpoint analysis and statistical derivation for submission (owned by biostatistics); TEA derivations are for review, not for the analysis dataset.
Medical decision-making. TEA produces suspicions for human adjudication and makes no clinical determination.

designPrinciples.principle:
Every numeric derivation and every rule verdict is computed by deterministic code from the rule pack. The LLM never decides whether a finding exists for a deterministic rule; it may only (a) adjudicate rules explicitly declared as judgement-based, (b) explain, and (c) draft language. A finding record always states which mode produced it.
Reproducibility is a validation prerequisite. It also means that when the LLM backend changes from a commercial API to a local GLM deployment, the review verdicts are bit-identical and no re-validation of the review logic is required — only of the narrative layer.

A finding is assembled from structured evidence (the exact records, values and computed quantities) first; narrative text is generated from that evidence and is not permitted to introduce facts absent from it. Narrative generation is a rendering step over a validated evidence object.

Each review point is a versioned declarative unit: identity, guideline basis, applicability, severity, logic, message templates, false-positive guards, and test cases. Adding a review point never requires modifying the orchestration.
The agent proposes; a qualified reviewer disposes. No query leaves the system without explicit human approval, and every disposition is recorded and fed back.
Output is written for a data manager who knows the trial but may not know the guideline clause. Every finding cites the guideline provision and states current data versus what would be expected.
The guideline provides defaults; the protocol overrides them. All thresholds, windows, counts and confirmation requirements are configuration, never constants in code.

Site-authored free text (query answers, comment fields, lesion descriptions) is data to be analysed, never instructions to be followed. It is passed to the model inside an explicit data envelope with injection defences.
A reviewer who receives 400 findings reviews none of them. Deduplication, query-history suppression and risk-based prioritisation are first-class components, not post-processing.

agentTopology.description: A supervising orchestrator drives a fixed, inspectable pipeline of specialised components. The topology is deliberately a pipeline rather than a free-form multi-agent conversation: the sequence of operations on regulated data must be predictable and replayable.
agentTopology.component: Reads source extracts (SDTM TU/TR/RS or EDC raw forms), maps them to the canonical model, normalises units, resolves lesion identity across visits, and records mapping provenance. Emits structural defects (unmappable records, broken lesion links) as findings in their own right.

Loads the study configuration: guideline version, indication, target lesion limits, confirmation requirement, assessment schedule and windows, imaging modality expectations, marker usage, iRECIST confirmation window. Produces a hash used in the provenance stamp.

Computes sum of diameters, nadir, percent changes, target/non-target/new-lesion responses, overall timepoint response, best overall response, and the iRECIST state sequence. Purely functional over the canonical model; fully unit-tested against worked examples.
Executes the rule pack against the canonical model plus derived values, producing raw findings with structured evidence.

Handles the small set of review points that are irreducibly qualitative: whether non-target worsening is "unequivocal", whether a new lesion description is unequivocal or equivocal, whether a lesion description implies non-measurability, whether a location text is anatomically consistent with the assigned organ. Returns a structured verdict with confidence and rationale; low-confidence verdicts are emitted as INFO-level "worth a look" rather than as issues.

Matches candidate findings against previously issued queries using a deterministic key plus LLM-assisted semantic matching for free-text queries. Classifies each finding as NEW, DUPLICATE_OPEN, ANSWERED_RESOLVED, ANSWERED_UNRESOLVED (escalate), or RECURRENT.

Collapses cascading findings (one root cause producing many downstream mismatches) into a primary finding with linked consequences, and scores by endpoint impact, severity, recurrence and query state.

Renders the five reviewer-facing elements from the evidence object using versioned prompt templates. Deterministic template fallback exists for every message so the system degrades gracefully when no LLM is available.
Persists the run, emits the findings in the output contract, and serves the web application and exports (XLSX/CSV/PDF).
Captures reviewer dispositions (accept, reject with reason, modify) and makes them available for rule tuning and for suppression of known-acceptable patterns.

humanInTheLoop.control: Findings are proposals. Reviewer disposition is mandatory before any external action.
Query text is a draft; the reviewer edits and approves before it is issued.
Rejections require a reason code, which feeds the false-positive analysis.
LLM-adjudicated findings are visually distinguished from deterministic findings in the UI.
No finding is auto-closed by the agent; closure is a human act recorded with attribution.

allowed.task: Narrative rendering of reviewer-facing text from a validated evidence object.
Drafting the initial query message in the sponsor's query style.
Semantic matching of a candidate finding to historical free-text queries.
Classifying free-text query answers (data will be corrected / data confirmed correct / clarification given / not addressed).
Adjudicating explicitly declared judgement rules, returning a structured verdict plus confidence.
Interpreting free-text lesion descriptions and comments for measurability and anatomical consistency signals.

forbidden.task: Performing arithmetic, percent change, nadir selection or table lookups.
Overriding, suppressing or creating a deterministic rule verdict.
Inferring a data value that is missing from the source.
Deciding the clinical management of a subject or the eligibility of a subject.
Acting on instructions found inside site-entered free text.

llmUsagePolicy.degradedMode: With no LLM configured, the agent runs deterministic rules only and renders messages from static templates. This mode is fully functional for the majority of review points and is the recommended configuration for environments where no model may see subject data.

knowledgeBase.description: Guideline knowledge is encoded twice, deliberately: as executable rules (authoritative for verdicts) and as a citable reference corpus (used to explain findings). The corpus is never used to decide anything.

source.citation: Therasse P, et al. J Natl Cancer Inst. 2000;92(3):205-216.

source.name: RECIST 1.1
source.citation: Eisenhauer EA, et al. Eur J Cancer. 2009;45(2):228-247.

source.name: iRECIST
source.citation: Seymour L, et al. Lancet Oncol. 2017;18(3):e143-e152.

source.name: RECIST 1.1 lymph node and FAQ clarifications
source.citation: RECIST Working Group publications and FAQ; to be pinned to specific versions at Step 2 sign-off.

source.name: Indication context notes
source.citation: Curated internal notes per indication (NSCLC, breast, etc.) governing which non-measurable presentations are common.

knowledgeBase.governance: Each corpus entry is versioned and hash-stamped. Findings cite the corpus entry id and clause, so a guideline clarification is traceable to the findings it affected.

interoperability.requirement: The agent must run unchanged against a commercial hosted model and a company-hosted local model, with GLM explicitly supported. This is treated as a first-class architectural constraint, not an adapter added later.
interoperability.approach: A single narrow provider interface — complete(messages, schema, options) → structured result — with adapters behind it. The application code never imports a vendor SDK directly.

adapter.name: OpenAI-compatible endpoint
adapter.note: Covers GLM served via an OpenAI-compatible gateway, vLLM, SGLang, Ollama and most internal gateways.

adapter.name: GLM (Zhipu) native endpoint
adapter.note: Kept separate from the generic adapter because parameter naming and tool-call semantics differ; see OQ-03 for the exact deployment.

interoperability.capabilityMatrix: Each adapter declares capabilities: native tool calling, JSON-schema constrained decoding, max context, streaming, determinism controls (temperature/seed), and cost class. The orchestrator selects a strategy per task from these capabilities rather than assuming the strongest one. Where constrained decoding is unavailable, the agent falls back to prompt-enforced JSON plus schema validation plus one bounded repair attempt, and finally to the deterministic template.

portabilityRules.rule: No provider-specific prompt syntax in templates; templates are plain text with typed slots.
Every LLM call declares an output JSON schema and is validated after the call; invalid output is a handled error, not an exception path.
Prompts are sized for a conservative context budget (see NFR-05) so a smaller local model is viable; evidence is pre-summarised deterministically rather than dumped.
A conformance test suite runs the same fixture set through every configured provider and asserts identical deterministic verdicts and acceptable narrative quality.

maintainability.practice: Rule pack as data: the rule catalog in the programming specification is the source artifact from which rule modules are generated/validated, so specification and code cannot drift.
One rule = one module + one test fixture set. Rules are pure functions of (canonical model, derived values, config) with no shared mutable state.
Layered structure with explicit boundaries: adapters (I/O) → domain (canonical model) → derivations → rules → assembly → presentation. Dependencies point inward only.
Configuration over branching: indication and protocol differences are parameters, not if-statements sprinkled through the rules.
Every new review point ships with: id, guideline citation, at least one positive and one negative test fixture, severity, and message templates. CI rejects rules missing any of these.
Golden-dataset regression: a curated dataset with known findings runs on every commit; any change in findings must be explicitly acknowledged in the rule pack change history.

dataModel.description: A canonical model sits between source data and the rules, so the rules never encode a source system's quirks. Two mapping profiles are planned: CDISC SDTM (TU/TR/RS) and EDC raw forms. The canonical model is the contract the rules and the web application both speak.

mapping.note: The exact EDC and form design must be confirmed; a mapping configuration file per study is expected rather than code.

reviewScope.description: Review points are organised into seven families, 84 review points in the current draft catalog. The full catalog with logic lives in TEA-SPEC-001; this section defines the families, their intent and their risk weighting so the sponsor can confirm coverage before the specification is detailed further.
reviewScope.family: Referential integrity between lesion identification and measurement records, duplicate lesions, nodal measurement axis, unit and precision consistency, visit chronology. Structural defects make every downstream check unreliable, so they are reported first and are the root of most finding cascades.

Eligibility of selected lesions, target counts and per-organ limits, measurability thresholds including nodal short axis, non-measurable presentations wrongly selected as target, previously irradiated lesions, baseline timing and completeness, duplicate lesions. An invalid baseline invalidates every downstream response for that subject and is expensive to fix late.

Sum recomputation, missing or not-done measurements without reason, non-evaluable handling, implausible measurement changes, unit and precision consistency, disappear/reappear handling, method and modality consistency, visit windows and assessment gaps. Measurement errors propagate silently into nadir, PD determination and PFS.

Target, non-target, new-lesion and overall response versus derivation; nadir correctness; the 20%-plus-5mm rule; CR conditions including nodal short axis; unequivocal non-target progression in the presence of measurable disease; the overall response table; confirmation; best overall response; progression date. These directly determine ORR, BOR, PFS and DoR — the primary and key secondary endpoints.

iUPD assignment, confirmation window compliance, iCPD criteria by progression driver, separate tracking of new lesion sums, resets after unconfirmed progression, treatment beyond progression documentation, and RECIST 1.1 versus iRECIST consistency. iRECIST errors are systematically under-detected because reviewers apply RECIST 1.1 habits to immunotherapy data.

Response versus disposition, death date, new anticancer therapy, radiotherapy or surgery on a target lesion, adverse event of disease progression, end-of-treatment reason, and investigator-versus-BICR discordance. The most defensible issues are those visible only when tumor data is read together with the rest of the trial.
Duplicate suppression, answered-but-unresolved escalation, recurrence across data cuts, site-level pattern detection, aging critical queries. Determines whether reviewers trust and adopt the tool.

layer.name: Adapters (inbound)
layer.responsibility: Read SDTM/EDC extracts and query history; validate structurally; map to canonical model. One module per source profile.

layer.name: Domain
layer.responsibility: Canonical entities, enumerations, protocol configuration. No I/O, no LLM.

layer.name: Derivations
layer.responsibility: Pure functions producing DerivedTimepoint and DerivedSubjectSummary. Exhaustively unit-tested.

layer.name: Rules
layer.responsibility: Declarative rule modules producing raw findings with structured evidence.

layer.name: Assembly
layer.responsibility: Adjudication, query reconciliation, deduplication, prioritisation, narrative composition.

layer.name: Ports (outbound)
layer.responsibility: LLM provider adapters, persistence, export, notification. Interface-defined, swappable.

layer.name: Presentation
layer.responsibility: Read-only API for the web application plus disposition write-back.

architecture.dependencyRule: Dependencies point inward. Rules may not import an LLM client or a database client.

option.rationale: Clinical programming teams already read Python; strong data tooling; simple packaging for on-premise deployment.

option.recommended: Pydantic models generated from the JSON contracts
option.rationale: Contract and code cannot drift; validation errors are themselves reportable findings.
Schema-first, generates OpenAPI for the front end.
Matches the interaction complexity of commercial review tools; large component ecosystem for data grids.
Run history, findings, dispositions and audit trail need relational integrity and retention.
Central place for redaction, rate limiting, logging and model pinning.
Required for the local-LLM, no-external-egress configuration.

mode.name: Cloud-assisted
mode.description: Commercial LLM API for narrative and adjudication; requires an approved data transfer path and de-identification.

mode.name: On-premise with local LLM
mode.description: GLM or equivalent served internally; no subject data leaves the network. Expected steady-state mode.

mode.name: Deterministic-only
mode.description: No LLM. Full rule coverage, template-rendered narratives. Usable where any model access is prohibited.

dataProtection.measure: De-identification/redaction layer before any external model call: subject identifiers pseudonymised, free text scrubbed of names and contact details, dates optionally offset with a reversible mapping held locally.
Configurable egress policy per study; deterministic-only mode enforced by configuration, not by convention.
No training or retention on submitted data; contractual and technical controls documented before first production use.
Prompt and completion logging is on by default for auditability, stored in the same trust boundary as the source data.

webApplication.designIntent: The application must support holistic review, not issue-by-issue triage in isolation. A reviewer must be able to move from an issue to the subject's whole tumor history and back without losing place, and must be able to see patterns across subjects and sites. The interaction vocabulary deliberately follows established clinical data review platforms (issue worklists with faceted filters, subject-level 360 views, listing-plus-detail panels, saved views, bulk disposition, query drafting inline, full audit trail) so that reviewers recognise the tool rather than learn it.

benchmarkPatterns.note: Patterns to emulate, drawn from widely used clinical data review and RBQM platforms
benchmarkPatterns.pattern: Issue worklist with faceted filtering, saved views and bulk actions.
Subject 360: one page collecting all data relevant to a subject's issues.
Listing-plus-detail: click a row, get the full evidence panel without navigating away.
Source-versus-derived side-by-side comparison with differences highlighted.
Longitudinal visualisations standard in oncology review: waterfall (best percent change), spider (percent change over time), swimmer (per-subject timeline of responses, queries and milestones).
Query drafting and issuance inline with the finding, with the draft editable before issue.
Signal/trend dashboard by site and by rule for risk-based monitoring.
Complete audit trail on every disposition and every version of the finding.

plannedScreens.screen: Run summary, findings by severity and family, top sites and subjects, open critical items, trend since last run.
Filterable, sortable, groupable list; columns for severity, family, subject, visit, query link status, priority; bulk disposition.
The five reviewer-facing elements, evidence table (observed vs expected), derivation trace, guideline citation, linked queries, query draft editor, disposition controls.
Lesion table across visits with a measurement heatmap, sum/nadir/percent-change chart, response timeline (reported vs derived), all findings and queries for the subject.
Waterfall, spider, swimmer plots; rule-level and site-level issue rates.
All TEA-originated queries and their lifecycle; recurrence and aging views.
Protocol configuration, active rule pack, model and prompt versions, run history with provenance.

webApplication.note: Screen inventory and component design are finalised in Step 4 and are subject to the sponsor's approval before any application code is written.

step.name: Development plan
step.entryCriteria: Requirements and considerations provided by the sponsor.
step.exitCriteria: Sponsor review completed; open questions OQ-01..OQ-14 answered or explicitly deferred with an accepted working assumption; plan approved at version 1.0.0.

activities.activity: Confirm review scope families and risk weighting.
Confirm data sources and mapping profile.
Confirm LLM deployment posture and data egress policy.

step.name: Programming specification
step.deliverable: TEA-SPEC-001, XML, including the machine-readable rule catalog and the input/output data contracts.
step.entryCriteria: Approved plan; confirmed data contracts; access to a de-identified sample extract.
step.exitCriteria: Every review point reviewed and either accepted, amended or removed by CDM and the Medical Monitor; rule pack frozen at version 1.0.0; each rule has agreed severity and message templates.

activities.activity: Line-by-line review of the rule catalog with CDM and Medical Monitor.
Confirm severity assignment and query wording conventions against sponsor standards.
Agree the golden dataset design and acceptance thresholds.

step.note: A draft is provided together with the plan so that the sponsor can see the concrete review logic while reviewing the plan; it will be revised after the Step 1 gate.

step.name: Prototype agent output on dummy data
step.deliverable: A curated dummy dataset exercising normal and exceptional cases, plus the agent's findings in the output contract, rendered for human reading.
step.exitCriteria: Reviewers confirm that the findings are correct, sufficiently explained, and correctly prioritised; measured precision/recall on the dummy set meets the agreed thresholds.

activities.activity: Build the dummy dataset with deliberately seeded issues, including at least: nodal CR handling, nadir-based PD with a sub-5mm increase, unconfirmed PR, iUPD not confirmed within window, new lesion in an unimaged region, disappear-and-reappear lesion, target lesion irradiated mid-study.
Run deterministic engine plus narrative layer under both a commercial model and a GLM configuration; compare verdict identity and narrative quality.
Reviewer scoring session; record every false positive and false negative with a reason.

step.name: Web application UI design
step.deliverable: High-level component design first, then a final UI design with concrete components and interaction states.
step.entryCriteria: Approved prototype output; agreed finding contract.
step.exitCriteria: Sponsor approves the final design; no application code before this approval.

activities.activity: High-level review: information architecture, screen inventory, navigation model.
Detailed design: component inventory, states (loading, empty, error, bulk selection), accessibility, responsive behaviour.
Usability walkthrough with two or three reviewers against realistic tasks.

step.name: Code generation
step.deliverable: Engine, rule pack, API and web application implementation with automated tests, plus the validation package.
step.exitCriteria: All rules implemented with tests; golden dataset regression green; conformance suite green across configured LLM providers; validation documentation complete.

activities.activity: Implement derivations first with exhaustive tests against published worked examples.
Implement rules in risk order (RS and IR families first).
Implement provider adapters and the conformance suite.
Implement the application against the approved design.

step.name: Finalisation
step.deliverable: Released application, user documentation, training material, support and change-control model.
step.entryCriteria: Successful user acceptance testing on at least one real (de-identified) study.
step.exitCriteria: Release approved; version 1.0.0 tagged across documents, rule pack and code; post-release monitoring in place.

functional.requirement: Re-derive all RECIST/iRECIST quantities per timepoint and per subject from lesion-level data.
Compare derived versus reported values and raise a finding on any discrepancy beyond configured tolerance.
Evaluate the full rule catalog per run, with rule applicability driven by guideline version and protocol configuration.
Emit for each finding the five reviewer-facing elements plus structured evidence and guideline citations.
Import query history and classify each finding's relation to it; suppress duplicates and escalate answered-but-unresolved cases.
Support selectable guideline rule packs (RECIST 1.0, 1.1, iRECIST) with per-study configuration overriding guideline defaults.
Run with any configured LLM provider, including a local GLM deployment, and in deterministic-only mode.
Persist every run with a full provenance stamp and support re-running a historical run for reproduction.
Record reviewer disposition per finding with attribution, timestamp and reason; maintain an immutable audit trail.
Deduplicate and cascade-group findings so one root cause is presented once with linked consequences.
Prioritise findings by a transparent, inspectable score.
Compare investigator and BICR assessments where both are collected and flag discordance.
Export findings to XLSX/CSV and a formatted report for offline review and for the trial master file.
Detect recurrence of the same issue across runs and across sites; surface site-level patterns.
Provide the subject 360 view with lesion history, derived quantities and longitudinal charts.
Support incremental runs that process only data changed since the previous snapshot.
Allow reviewer-authored suppression rules for known-acceptable patterns, with expiry and audit.

nonFunctional.requirement: Given the same input snapshot, configuration and versions, deterministic findings are identical across runs and across LLM providers.
Adding a review point requires only a new rule module, its fixtures and a catalog entry; no engine change. Verified by a CI check.
A study of 500 subjects with 12 assessments each completes a deterministic full run in under 5 minutes on standard hardware; narrative generation is parallelised and incremental.
Web application list views respond within 2 seconds at 10,000 findings.
No single LLM call exceeds a 32k-token prompt budget, so that smaller local models remain viable; evidence is pre-summarised deterministically.
Role-based access; subject data encrypted at rest and in transit; egress policy enforced by configuration.
Audit trail meeting ALCOA+ expectations on all human actions and all agent runs; records retained per sponsor retention policy.
A reviewer can go from a finding to full context and back in a single click, with no loss of filter state.
An LLM outage degrades the system to deterministic-only mode rather than failing the run.
Every run emits metrics: rule hit counts, adjudication rates, model latency and failure rates, disposition outcomes.
Query text templates support multiple languages where sites require them.

regulatoryAndQuality.requirement: The system is decision support; a qualified human makes every determination and issues every query.
Risk-based validation consistent with GAMP 5 (2nd edition) and the FDA Computer Software Assurance approach, scaled to the system's intended use and impact on data integrity.
Where the system is used in a GxP process, 21 CFR Part 11 and EU Annex 11 expectations apply to audit trail, access control and record retention.
Specification-to-test traceability: every requirement and every rule traces to at least one test case.
Change control: rule pack and prompt changes follow documented review and approval, with impact assessment on previously issued findings.
Alignment with ICH E6(R3) expectations on risk-proportionate, quality-by-design monitoring approaches.
Data privacy assessment completed before any subject data reaches an external model; deterministic-only or on-premise mode used until it is.

risk.description: The model fabricates or subtly misstates facts in the narrative, and a reviewer acts on the narrative rather than the evidence.
risk.mitigation: Narrative is rendered from a validated evidence object; numbers in the text are injected from computed values, not generated; the evidence table is always displayed adjacent to the narrative; template fallback available.
risk.residual: Low-moderate; mitigated further by reviewer training that the evidence panel is authoritative.

risk.description: False positives erode trust and the tool is abandoned.
risk.mitigation: False-positive guards per rule; query-history suppression; prioritisation; Step 3 tuning against a scored dummy dataset; mandatory rejection reason codes feeding rule tuning; INFO tier for low-confidence signals.
risk.residual: Moderate; managed as an ongoing metric, not a one-time fix.

risk.description: False negatives: reviewers assume full coverage and stop looking, while the agent misses an issue class.
risk.mitigation: Explicit, published coverage statement per rule family; the UI states what was checked and what was not; recall measured on the golden dataset; manual review retained for uncovered areas.
risk.residual: Moderate. Requires clear communication that TEA augments rather than replaces review.

risk.description: Subject data leaves the approved boundary through an external model call.
risk.mitigation: Egress policy enforced in configuration; de-identification layer; on-premise GLM as the steady-state mode; deterministic-only mode available; prompt logging inside the trust boundary.
risk.residual: Low once the privacy assessment (REG-07) is complete.

risk.description: Prompt injection via site-entered free text (query answers, comments) redirecting the agent.
risk.mitigation: Free text is passed inside an explicit data envelope with instructions to treat it as data; output is schema-constrained; the LLM cannot alter deterministic verdicts or trigger actions; suspicious instruction-like content is itself flagged.
risk.residual: Low, because the model has no tool authority over external systems.

risk.description: Genuinely ambiguous guideline areas (reappearing lesions, too-small-to-measure conventions, unequivocal progression thresholds) are implemented one way and the sponsor expects another.
risk.mitigation: All ambiguous points are surfaced as explicit configuration with a documented default and are listed for decision at the Step 2 gate; the specification records the interpretation chosen and its rationale.
risk.residual: Low after Step 2 sign-off, provided protocol-specific decisions are captured per study.

risk.description: Each protocol deviates from guideline defaults; hard-coding one study's rules makes the tool unusable for the next.
risk.mitigation: Protocol configuration object with every threshold externalised; configuration is reviewed and signed off per study; configuration hash recorded in provenance.

risk.description: Fields needed by some rules (slice thickness, prior irradiation, scan dates per modality) are not collected.
risk.mitigation: Rules declare required fields; unavailable fields deactivate the rule with an explicit "not evaluated" statement in the coverage report rather than a silent pass.
risk.residual: Low, but reduces coverage; feeds a recommendation on eCRF design.

risk.description: A local GLM deployment lacks reliable structured output or tool calling, producing malformed responses.
risk.mitigation: Capability matrix per adapter; schema validation with bounded repair; deterministic template fallback; conformance suite run per provider before use.
risk.residual: Low; worst case is degraded narrative quality, never a wrong verdict.

risk.description: Validation effort is underestimated because the system touches endpoint-critical data.
risk.mitigation: Validation approach agreed with QA at the Step 1 gate; risk-based scope; the deterministic/LLM split confines the hardest validation questions to the narrative layer, which does not affect verdicts.

risk.description: Reviewers treat agent output as authoritative (automation bias) and stop applying judgement.
risk.mitigation: Findings are phrased as suspicions requiring confirmation; confidence and determination mode are always visible; training emphasises accountability; rejection is a first-class, frictionless action.

risk.description: Query flooding: a systemic data-entry misunderstanding at one site generates hundreds of findings, overwhelming the site.
risk.mitigation: Cascade grouping; site-level pattern detection promoting many findings into one systemic signal; reviewer-controlled issuance; rate awareness in the dashboard.

risk.description: Pressure to add other criteria (Lugano, RANO, mRECIST, PCWG3) before the core is stable.
risk.mitigation: Rule pack architecture makes later addition cheap; explicit out-of-scope statement for release 1; a decision gate for each addition.

risk.description: Specification and implementation drift as rules are patched under time pressure.
risk.mitigation: Rule catalog in the specification is the source artifact for the rule pack; CI check asserts that every implemented rule exists in the catalog at the same version and vice versa.

validationAndCompliance.approach: Risk-based, proportionate to intended use. TEA does not modify source data and does not determine subject management; its risk is that it misleads a reviewer or misses an issue. Validation therefore concentrates on the deterministic derivations and rules (high rigour, full test coverage, documented expected results) and treats the narrative layer as a supporting function verified for accuracy of injected values and absence of unsupported claims.
validationAndCompliance.activity: Requirements → specification sections → rules → test cases → test results.

Every derivation function and every rule, with positive, negative and boundary fixtures. Boundary tests explicitly include the 20%/5 mm PD boundary, the 30% PR boundary, 10 mm and 15 mm nodal thresholds, and the iRECIST 5 mm confirmation increment.
A curated dataset with a signed-off expected finding list; run on every commit; changes require acknowledgement in the rule pack change history.
The same fixture set through every configured LLM provider; deterministic verdicts must be identical; narrative outputs scored against a rubric.
Reviewers run realistic tasks on a de-identified real study; acceptance criteria agreed at the Step 3 gate.
Environment, configuration, access control, backup and audit trail verification, scaled per the deployment mode.
Rule pack effectiveness reviewed per data cut using disposition statistics; model and prompt versions re-verified when changed.

referenceFrameworks.framework: GAMP 5 (2nd edition) risk-based approach to computerised systems
FDA guidance on Computer Software Assurance for production and quality system software
21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11 (audit trail, access control, records)

versionControl.principle: Everything that can change a finding is versioned and stamped into that finding.

versionedArtifact.name: Rule pack
versionedArtifact.note: Independent of the specification version so a wording fix does not force a rule pack release

versionControl.branching: Trunk-based with short-lived feature branches; rule pack changes require an explicit reviewer from CDM or Medical Monitoring in addition to a technical reviewer.
versionControl.impactAssessment: Any MAJOR rule pack change triggers a documented impact assessment on findings already issued under the previous version.

metric.name: Precision (finding acceptance rate)
metric.target: ≥ 0.80 for CRITICAL and MAJOR at release

metric.name: Recall on golden dataset
metric.target: 1.00 for deterministic rules; ≥ 0.85 for judgement rules

metric.name: Duplicate suppression accuracy
metric.target: ≥ 0.95, with zero incorrect suppression of CRITICAL findings

metric.name: Narrative faithfulness
metric.definition: Sampled findings whose narrative contains no statement unsupported by the evidence object
metric.target: ≥ 0.98, audited per release and per model change

metric.name: Time to review
metric.definition: Median reviewer minutes per subject per data cut versus baseline
metric.target: Measured at UAT; improvement is the business case

recommendations.recommendation: Keep the deterministic/LLM split absolute. It is what makes local-LLM portability, validation and reproducibility tractable at once. Resist the temptation to let the model "just decide" borderline cases; make them configuration instead.

Treat the rule catalog in the specification as the source of truth from which rule modules are generated or validated. This is the single most effective defence against specification drift over a multi-year maintenance life.

Invest in the golden dataset early, during Step 3. It is simultaneously the acceptance criterion, the regression suite and the training material, and it costs far less to build before implementation than after.

Start with one indication and one protocol, and only then generalise. Coverage breadth on a single well-understood study is more convincing to reviewers than shallow coverage on many. Recommended first target: an immunotherapy study using iRECIST, because that is where manual review is weakest and the payoff is largest.

Report coverage, not just findings. Each run should state which rules ran, which were deactivated for missing data, and which subjects were not evaluable — so a clean report is informative rather than merely empty.

Feed eCRF design back into the process. Several high-value checks depend on fields that are often not collected (prior irradiation flag, slice thickness, per-modality scan dates, lesion state vocabulary). Collecting them is cheap at study start-up and unlocks whole rule families.

Run TEA against the BICR stream as well as the investigator stream where both exist. Investigator-versus-BICR discordance detection is often the highest-yield single check in studies where BICR drives the primary endpoint.
Make rejection cheap and informative. Reviewer rejection reasons are the primary tuning signal; a free-text-only rejection wastes that signal, so use a short coded list plus optional text.

Pin model versions per study and record them. A silent model upgrade mid-study changes narrative behaviour; the deterministic verdicts will not move, but reviewers will notice and lose confidence if the change is unexplained.
Plan for a "reviewer notebook" feature: reviewer-authored notes attached to a subject that persist across runs. In practice this is what reviewers ask for first once issue triage works.

question.text: Will TEA consume CDISC SDTM (TU/TR/RS) extracts, raw EDC exports, or both? If EDC, which system and can a de-identified sample extract plus the eCRF specification be provided?
question.workingAssumption: Both profiles are supported; SDTM is implemented first because it is standardised.

question.text: What is the source, format and refresh cadence of the query history, and does it contain a machine-readable link to the queried form/field/record? Should TEA-approved queries be written back automatically, or exported for manual issuance?
question.workingAssumption: Query history is imported as a periodic extract with subject, visit, form, field, text, status and dates; issuance is manual export in release 1.

question.text: Which GLM version and serving stack will be used internally (native API, OpenAI-compatible gateway, vLLM), what context window and throughput are available, and does it support constrained JSON output or tool calling?
question.workingAssumption: An OpenAI-compatible gateway with JSON mode but without reliable constrained decoding; prompts are designed for a 32k budget with schema validation and repair.

question.text: For the first target study: is response confirmation required, what is the assessment interval and window, what is the minimum SD duration, is iRECIST in use and with what confirmation window, and are tumor markers used in the CR definition?
question.workingAssumption: Guideline defaults as listed in ProtocolConfig; confirmation not required; iRECIST confirmation window 4–8 weeks.

question.text: Which indications should release 1 cover, and are there indication-specific conventions in use (for example bone-only disease handling in breast cancer, pleural effusion and cavitation handling in NSCLC)?
question.workingAssumption: NSCLC and breast cancer, with indication context notes limited to measurability guidance.

question.text: Is RECIST 1.0 support genuinely needed for active studies, and should mRECIST/Choi/RANO/Lugano/PCWG3 be on the roadmap?
question.workingAssumption: RECIST 1.0 supported as a rule pack for legacy studies; other criteria out of scope for release 1, architecture kept open.

question.text: Are there mandated platform, language, hosting or authentication standards the solution must adopt (for example an existing internal web platform, SSO provider, or approved database)?
question.workingAssumption: Python engine, React front end, PostgreSQL, containerised on-premise deployment.

question.text: Which roles need which permissions (data manager, medical monitor, CRA, biostatistician, read-only auditor), and is there a required segregation of duties between the person who accepts a finding and the person who issues the query?
question.workingAssumption: Four roles: reviewer, approver, read-only, administrator; approval and issuance may be performed by the same reviewer.

question.text: Are the proposed precision and recall targets acceptable, and who signs off the golden dataset as the acceptance basis?
question.workingAssumption: Targets as stated in qualityAndMetrics; golden dataset signed off jointly by CDM lead and Medical Monitor.

question.text: May subject-level data be sent to a commercial LLM API under existing agreements, or must the first release run on-premise or deterministic-only?
question.workingAssumption: On-premise or deterministic-only until a privacy assessment is complete.

question.text: Do any participating sites require query text in a language other than English?
question.workingAssumption: English only in release 1; templates structured to allow localisation later.

question.text: How often should reviews run (on demand, nightly, per data cut), and what are the expected subject and assessment volumes at peak?
question.workingAssumption: Nightly incremental plus on-demand; sizing per NFR-03.

question.text: Is independent central review data available to TEA, and at what latency relative to investigator data? Should investigator-versus-BICR discordance be reported, given that some sponsors deliberately keep the streams separate?
question.workingAssumption: Discordance detection is built but disabled by configuration unless the sponsor enables it.

question.text: What validation deliverables does QA expect for a decision-support system of this type, and is an existing internal AI/ML governance procedure applicable?
question.workingAssumption: Risk-based validation package as described; to be confirmed with QA at the Step 1 gate.

assumptions.assumption: Source data is available as a periodic extract; TEA does not connect directly to the production EDC.
Lesion identity is stable across visits and carries a usable link identifier; where it is not, the ingestion layer raises structural findings.
Protocol configuration can be obtained and signed off per study before the first run.
Reviewers, not the agent, remain accountable for every query issued and every issue closed.
Imaging source documents and DICOM are out of reach; all checks operate on collected data.

glossary.term: Best overall response — the best timepoint response recorded from treatment start until progression, subject to confirmation rules.
The smallest sum of diameters recorded on study, including baseline; the reference for progression.
A lesion recorded at baseline but not measured quantitatively; assessed qualitatively.
iRECIST unconfirmed and confirmed progressive disease.
Non-target worsening substantial enough to warrant progression, comparable in magnitude to what would be required in measurable disease.
One suspected issue produced by the agent for human review.
The versioned collection of review points applicable to a guideline version.
The stable identity of an issue across runs, independent of the run that produced it.
